name: smtp-utf8-ulabel-domain-permit-valid
description: An A-label rfc822Name permit (xn--e1afmkfd.xn--p1ai) with a SmtpUTF8Mailbox SAN whose domain is in U-label form (пример.рф). Under RFC 8398 this is the conforming pairing - the matcher was expected to convert the constraint A-label to U-label and compare. RFC 9598 §3 reversed that rule and now forbids U-label form in SmtpUTF8Mailbox SANs, so a strict-RFC-9598 reading would reject this leaf.
notes: Under RFC 8398 (May 2018) this was the canonical EAI shape: SmtpUTF8Mailbox SAN domain in U-label form, rfc822 constraint in A-label form, matcher converts the constraint A-label to U-label and compares octet-for-octet.

RFC 9598 (Feb 2024, obsoletes RFC 8398) inverted the rule: SmtpUTF8Mailbox domains MUST now be in A-label form. So the SAN here is no longer spec-conformant; a strict-RFC-9598 implementation should reject the SAN at parse time or reject the chain at constraint-match time.
OpenSSL's nc_email_eai still implements RFC 8398 (the function comment cites that RFC), so it accepts this chain.
Go accepts vacuously - it does not apply rfc822 name constraints to SmtpUTF8Mailbox otherName SANs at all.
Companion to `smtp-utf8-alabel-domain-permit-valid`, which is the RFC 9598-conformant counterpart (A-label/A-label, octet-for-octet match).
